sm: Georgia Howe opens Evening Wire for Friday, November 20th, with John Bickley out on vacation. Poland has accused Russia of intentional provocation after missiles from an overnight offensive of about 400 drones and over 100 missiles landed on or crossed into Polish territory. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said what landed came from Russia and does not look like an accident, while Russia calls the incidents unintentional. The strikes also hit the Austrian embassy in Ukraine, and France called an emergency UN Security Council meeting. Separately, national cyber director Sean Cairncross is stepping down so the Senate can confirm a successor before Democrats take control, with Kirsten Davies filling in. The Senate also advanced a permitting reform bill 62 to 33. Anthropic's record IPO failed to stop a market sell-off, with the S&P down more than 6 percent for the week and Nvidia's losses a major factor. Finally, New York's transportation workers union sued over Mayor Mamdani's ban on horse-drawn carriages, which he defended by saying the city has changed.

Daily Wire editor Zach Jewell reports that crime in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta has surged since 70,000 to 80,000 migrants crossed from Morocco in late July, with sharply higher reports of sexual assaults, firearm attacks and knife attacks. A 4.2 magnitude earthquake shook the Los Angeles area early Friday with no significant damage reported. A Virginia district closed all 29 schools through Thanksgiving after finding more than 500 employees were never screened against the child abuse registry. Fourteen people were charged in a train robbery ring accused of stealing over 22.5 million dollars in goods. Finally, a Maryland synagogue asked the Fourth Circuit to block a Montgomery County ban on firearms within 100 yards of public assemblies, noting congregants can carry inside but not on their walk to services. The hosts then recap earlier coverage and say the show returns tomorrow morning.
sg: Crime, Schools, and Synagogue Firearms Ban
